context: Server metrics dashboard with 4 KPI summary cards (each using a different mini-chart type: spark bar, spark area, win/loss, bullet) and an 18-row sortable table with three sparkline columns per row (CPU, memory, requests) plus numeric columns for error rate, P99 latency, and uptime. Sparklines animate in with a staggered row reveal on load.
first_impression: Clean and scannable — color restraint and red error highlights let anomalies surface quickly without overwhelming the viewer.
what_works: Shared Y-axis domains (0–100) across all CPU and memory sparklines enable direct row-to-row comparison without mental rescaling; red highlighting on error-rate outliers (db-replica-02 at 4.93, worker-batch-01 at 2.28) creates an immediate visual hierarchy that routes attention to the right rows. The staggered animation reveal (40ms per row) aids object constancy without creating visual chaos across 54 simultaneous animation targets.
what_doesnt: The four KPI cards each use a different chart type (spark bar, spark area, win/loss, bullet) — this variety signals 'look, different encodings' rather than 'here is your fleet at a glance,' adding chart-literacy overhead before the viewer reaches the table. The in-table sparklines are 80×18px, which makes the request bar-chart column (48 bars crammed into 80px) nearly unreadable as individual bars — it functions more as a texture than a data series, undermining the per-row comparison it was designed to support.
